pool.text: The town of the settlement was granted a formal charter.
Thomas de la Warre founded a collegiate church for the parish.
The Manchester Grammar School was established in the city as a private school.
Chetham's Library opened and remains open as a public reference library.
The Bridgewater Canal opened, bringing coal from mines to the centre.
Richard Arkwright began construction of the first cotton mill.
Developers created the world's first stored-program computer known as the Manchester Baby.
Anthony Burgess lived in Manchester while writing the dystopian satire A Clockwork Orange.
The first edition of Top of the Pops was broadcast from Dickenson Road Studios.
The Manchester Business School offered the first Master of Business Administration course in the UK.
Manchester Metropolitan University was formed as Manchester Polytechnic upon a merger of colleges.
The Northern School of Music and Royal Manchester College of Music merged to form the RNCM.
The Canal Street area has hosted the Manchester Pride festival each August since this year.
The band Oasis formed within the city of Manchester.
The Manchester Metrolink opened, providing a modern light rail tram system.
Manchester Polytechnic gained university status and absorbed a college in South Cheshire.
The university became a founding member of the Russell Group of universities.
A lorry bomb was set off by the IRA in Corporation Street.
The 2500 seat Bridgewater Hall opened as a major classical music venue.
The Beetham Tower was completed as a tall residential building.
